_about: One rule per (service, table.field) construct the suite reads (inventory.json). class: as_is (a public API call creates it exactly), change (possible with the stated change), no (not with ordinary accounts). Tags name the change: date_shift (a server-set time: it becomes the seeding time, and the request's date words are rewritten to it), rename (the service assigns ids, emails, logins or identifiers; requests that name them are rewritten), ui (a manual step in the web interface), plan:<plan> (a paid plan), workspace (a Google Workspace account), pilot (documented as internal or not documented; try it before relying on it). People are handled apart: every person a seed names needs an account, and people who author, own, modify, react, resolve or answer need that account's own API token (counted per test in classify.py). A table's '*' rule covers its structural fields (ids and joins). Checks that need the seed itself (Linear team count, Box collection count, Calendar event types and ACL scopes, attendee rooms) are in classify.py.

channels.*.why: conversations.create, setTopic, setPurpose, archive; conversations.open for DMs and group DMs with the bot

channels.created_at.why: a channel's creation time is when it is created; no API argument sets it

channel_members.*.why: conversations.invite by the bot or a member

messages.*.why: chat.postMessage (text, blocks, thread_ts); each author posts with their own user token

messages.created_at.why: a message's ts is its posting time: 'No argument sets the post time'. The workspace import tool may keep old timestamps but the help pages do not say so, and a Free workspace hides messages older than 90 days

message_reactions.*.why: reactions.add with the reacting person's user token

users.*.why: one Slack account per seeded person; each sets its own profile (real_name, display_name, title) with users.profile.set and its own user token

users.email.why: an account's email is its real address; requests that name an email are rewritten

users.username.why: the handle comes with the account; an Owner's or Admin's token can change usernames, and changing another person's profile needs a paid plan; otherwise rewrite the request to the real handles

users.timezone.why: users.profile.set has no time-zone field; each account sets it in its preferences

users.is_bot.why: each seeded bot is a Slack app with a bot user, installed by hand; a Free workspace allows 10 apps

users.is_active.why: an owner deactivates the account in the admin UI, on every plan; its messages stay

user_teams.role.why: owners and admins are promoted in the admin UI; guest accounts exist only on paid plans

issues.*.why: issueCreate sets title, description, priority, estimate, dueDate, assignee, state, project, cycle, labels, parent, milestone and subscribers; the creator is the key's owner

issues.createdAt.why: IssueCreateInput.createdAt: 'e.g. if importing from another system. Must be a time in the past.'

issues.completedAt.why: IssueCreateInput.completedAt: 'Must be a time in the past and after createdAt.'

issues.updatedAt.why: updatedAt is the last meaningful update, set by Linear

issues.identifier.why: identifiers (TEAM-n) are assigned in creation order; create in order or rewrite the request

comments.*.why: commentCreate (body, parent, issue) with the author's key; resolved with the resolver's key

comments.createdAt.why: CommentCreateInput.createdAt: 'Must be a time in the past.'

comments.resolvedAt.why: a thread is resolved when commentResolve runs; no input sets the time

cycles.*.why: cycleCreate sets teamId, startsAt, endsAt, name (and completedAt). Whether cycles wholly in the past are accepted is not documented

cycles.number.why: Cycle.number 'is assigned automatically by the database and cannot be set on creation': create the cycles in number order (a test naming cycle 11 needs 11 cycles) or rewrite the request

attachments.*.why: attachmentCreate (title, url, subtitle); the source type follows the url; the creator is the key's owner

documents.*.why: documentCreate (title, content, projectId); the creator is the key's owner

projects.*.why: projectCreate (name, description, priority, lead, dates, status, teams); health through projectUpdateCreate

project_milestones.status.why: no input sets a milestone's status; Linear derives it

workflow_states.*.why: every team gets the default states; workflowStateCreate for others

teams.*.why: teamCreate (name, key, description, parent); the Free plan allows 2 teams (checked per test)

teams.parentId.why: TeamCreateInput.parentId exists; the pricing page lists sub-teams as '1 level' on Free and Basic and '5 levels' on Business, which does not say whether one level of nesting is allowed on Free

teams.private.why: 'Private teams and guests' come with Business; TeamCreateInput.private is 'Internal'

team_memberships.owner.why: TeamMembershipCreateInput.owner is marked 'Internal'; team owners may have to be set in the team's settings

users.*.why: one Linear member per seeded person; each sets its own name, displayName, statusLabel and timezone with userUpdate

users.email.why: an account's email is its real address; requests that name an email are rewritten

users.admin.why: 'On Free plans, all members are treated as admins'; admin roles start at Basic

users.app.why: an app user is an OAuth application acting as itself; one app per seeded app user

users.active.why: an admin suspends the account; User.active is 'active or disabled (suspended)'

box_files.*.why: upload and PUT /files/{id}: name, description, tags, lock, shared link, parent; extension and size follow the uploaded file; people act through App Users and the As-User header

box_files.version_number.why: the free developer plan keeps '1 file version'

box_files.created_at.why: created_at is 'when the file was created on Box'; upload sets only content_created_at

box_files.modified_at.why: set by Box when the file changes

box_files.collections.why: only the Favorites collection exists (checked per test)

box_folders.*.why: POST /folders and PUT /folders/{id}: name, description, tags, shared link, parent; size follows the contents

box_folders.created_at.why: set by Box when the folder is created

box_folders.modified_at.why: set by Box when the folder changes

box_folders.collections.why: only the Favorites collection exists (checked per test)

box_collections.*.why: 'Currently, only the favorites collection is supported' (checked per test)

box_comments.*.why: POST /comments on a file or a comment, as its author

box_comments.created_at.why: set by Box when the comment is posted

box_tasks.*.why: POST /tasks (action, message, due_at, completion rule) as its creator; completed by its assignees

box_tasks.created_at.why: set by Box when the task is created

box_task_assignments.*.why: POST /task_assignments by the task's creator; resolved by the assignee

box_hubs.*.why: Box Hubs needs 'Box Hubs enabled for your enterprise', for 'Enterprise and Enterprise Plus customers'

box_users.*.why: App Users created by the app, named as the seed names them

box_users.login.why: App Users get generated logins and real accounts real emails; requests that name a login are rewritten

calendars.*.why: calendars.insert and patch (summary, description, location, timeZone); 'The authenticated user for the request is made the data owner'

calendar_list_entries.*.why: calendarList.patch sets hidden, selected, summaryOverride; accessRole follows the owner's ACL grant

calendar_acl_rules.*.why: acl.insert by the calendar's owner (user scope); group and domain scopes are checked per test

calendar_events.*.why: events.insert with any start and end, past ones included (the 2018 dates the Calendar tests use); status, visibility, transparency, color, recurrence, all-day; creator is the creating account; organizer is the calendar it is created on, or set by events.import, which also sets iCalUID

calendar_events.event_type.why: focus time, out of office and working location events exist only on primary calendars, and only for work or school accounts (checked per test)

calendar_events.hangout_link.why: a Meet link is generated through conferenceData; hangoutLink itself is read-only

calendar_event_attendees.*.why: attendees are added by the organizer; an attendee's response comes from the attendee's own account

calendar_event_attendees.resource.why: rooms are a Workspace customer's calendar resources, created by an administrator with the 'Buildings and resources administrator' privilege (checked per test)
